successors.name: Sumerian city-states
successors.text: the southern alluvium, Cliopatria's first row

successors.name: Elam
successors.text: Susiana, where "Proto-Elamite in southwestern Iran" replaces Urukean influence

ledger.x: 4000 BCE: the Uruk period opens in the south, the age of the first cities.
3800 BCE: Middle Uruk; Urukean settlers reach the Zagros, the Khabur and the upper Euphrates.
3500 BCE: the Uruk expansion at its peak.
3400 BCE: Cliopatria's Sumerian City-States row begins and takes the alluvium from the culture layer.
3200 BCE: Susa turns Proto-Elamite and Cliopatria's Elam row begins.
3200 BCE: the Uruk colonies are deserted.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture: the core is the alluvium, the outposts are radii around excavated colonies; nothing is a frontier.
